item.title: Research and Teaching Assistant (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Business Administration - Munich School of Management

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-04-19T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>Research and teaching activities of the Institute for Finance & Banking headed by Prof. Dr. Ralf Elsas-Nicolle cover the fields of banking and corporate finance. The research profile is international and predominantly empirically oriented.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>Excellent academic record and university degree in Business Administration/Economics or a related field with quantitative orientation at Master's level</li> <li>Outstanding knowledge in Financial Economics and Mathematics and/or Data Science</li> <li>Strong interest in scientific research</li> <li>Passion for teaching and lecturing</li> <li>High motivation and enthusiasm for efficient team work</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<p>We offer you an interesting and responsible position with good opportunities for further training and development in a terrific team and academically stimulating environment. You receive individual career support, a fair salary according to <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">TV-L</a>, have flexible work hours and the opportunity to collaborate with companies and internationally renowned scientists. You will also have the chance to participate in training programs and conferences worldwide. The opportunity to study towards a PhD at IFB is given as part of the position which is initially limited to a period of three years with the possibility of extension. Your workplace is centrally located in Munich and is easily accessible by public transportation. We actively promote gender equality.</p>

Contact: <p>Please send your application as a single PDF file, max. 10 MB, by e-mail addressed to Prof. Dr. Ralf Elsas-Nicolle (<a href="mailto:ifb@som.lmu.de">ifb@som.lmu.de</a>) <strong>not later than April 19, 2026</strong>.</p>

item.title: PhD Student or PostDoc (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Statistics

Remuneration: TV-L

Application deadline: 2026-03-06T22:59:57+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>As an AI chair at the Mathematical Institute of the Faculty of Mathematics, Computer Science and Statistics at Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, the Chair for Mathematical Foundations of <a href="https://www.ai.math.uni-muenchen.de">Artificial Intelligence</a> is part of the High-Tech Agenda of the Free State of Bavaria. Current research focuses include (1) reliable AI, e.g. expressivity, generalization ability and explanatory work of (graph) neural networks, and (2) sustainable AI, e.g. spiking neural networks as an energy-efficient variant of classic neural networks. We are also working on mathematically based AI methods for inverse problems and PDEs, as well as AI-based learning of physical laws; with applications in the fields of medicine, robotics and telecommunications. The chair is responsible in a leading role for various large-scale initiatives at the LMU as well as in the Munich area, including the AI-HUB@LMU, the Konrad Zuse School of Excellence in Reliable AI, the planned Munich House of AI as well as the Bavaria-Saxony project “Next Generation AI Computing (gAIn)”.</p> <p>The position to be filled is part of the project “KI-ROBUST: Artificial Intelligence and Robust Optimization for Dealing with Uncertainties in Radiation Therapy”. In this interdisciplinary project, we are developing an AI system that will shape radiotherapy of the future: reliable, trustworthy and directly clinically relevant. Our technology is intended to fundamentally improve treatment planning by automatically and precisely contouring tumors - even with particularly complex or irregular shapes. At the same time, the system provides clear information about diagnostic uncertainties so that doctors can concentrate specifically on the crucial areas. This not only reduces the effort required for consistent contouring, but also makes a key contribution to making cancer treatments faster, safer and ultimately more effective</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>You have a very good university degree in mathematics, computer science or a comparable subject, preferably with a focus on an area of mathematical fundamentals and/or the explainability of artificial intelligence</li> <li>You have very good programming skills</li> <li>You are fluent in spoken and written communication in German and English</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>An exciting and responsible job in a highly topical research area with excellent training and development opportunities and the possibility of a PhD</li> <li>Embedding in the unique Munich AI ecosystem with numerous interdisciplinary networking and cooperation opportunities</li> <li>A pleasant, collegial working atmosphere in a highly international department</li> <li>A workplace in a central location in Munich that is very easy to reach by public transport</li> </ul> <p>Remuneration is based on appropriate qualifications and professional experience up to <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">TV-L E13</a>. The LMU strives to increase the proportion of women in academic staff and expressly encourages qualified women to apply.</p>

Contact: <p>We look forward to receiving your application, including the usual documents (cover letter, CV, copies of certificates and diplomas, list of publications, contact details of two people for letters of support), <strong>by</strong> <strong>March 6th 2026</strong>, via the "Online Application" function.<br /> For any questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Gitta Kutyniok.</p>

item.title: Postdoctoral researcher on Reconciliation of land fluxes between global models and national greenhouse gas inventories (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Geosciences

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-03-15T23:00:37+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Schmidt Sciences Virtual Institute of the Carbon Cycle aims to reduce uncertainty in the global carbon cycle by an order of magnitude in order to inform effective climate policy and solutions. To this end, an international project led by the University of Exeter, the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU) and the University of Maryland has started a project on Combining LAnd-use, modeling and Remote-sensing to Transform carbon budgets (<a href="https://clarityvicc.org/">CLARiTy</a>). We offer a joined postdoc position at the LMU in Munich, Germany and the Joint Research Centre in Ispra, Italy at the interface of science and policy in CLARiTy.</p> <p>The Chair for Physical Geography and Land Use Systems (Prof. Julia Pongratz) at LMU’s Department of Geography investigates the interactions between humans, ecosystems and climate. Our group develops and applies the latest generation of carbon cycle and climate models and integrates them with Earth observations. We lead the estimates of the land-use carbon fluxes in the annual Global Carbon Budgets and are involved in a range of national and international projects that aim to provide the science basis for pathways to limit global warming in line with the Paris Agreement. The position plans a period of up to two years as Visiting Scientist at the Joint Research Centre (Ispra, VA, Italy), under the supervision of Dr. Giacomo Grassi. The JRC is the European Commission’s in-house science service, providing independent scientific evidence to support EU policies. In the area of climate change, the JRC works on reconciling land carbon flux estimates between global models and national greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories, which often differ due to varying definitions of anthropogenic land-use emissions and managed land. By analysing these conceptual differences and developing harmonisation and translation approaches, the JRC helps improve the consistency and comparability of land-use emissions and removals, supporting robust assessments of climate progress under the Paris Agreement. To this aim, the JRC has promoted an expert meeting under the <a href="https://www.ipcc-nggip.iges.or.jp/public/mtdocs/2407_EM_Land.html">IPCC</a> and developed a platform to <a href="https://forest-observatory.ec.europa.eu/carbon/fluxes">compare land use emissions data and stimulate a dialogue across communities</a>.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>You hold a Ph.D., or will soon finish your Ph.D., in a natural science subject (geography, environmental science, physics or similar).</li> <li>a track record of effectively communicating research results (commensurate with career stage)</li> <li>good programming skills (provide details)</li> <li>very good communication skills in English (our working language)</li> <li>Training or experience in ecosystem modeling and/or national inventories is highly desirable, but not essential.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>the opportunity to be part of a dynamic, internationally connected team working at the forefront of Earth system science</li> <li>E13 TV-L position, commensurate with work experience, for up to three years, starting May 2026 or soon thereafter</li> <li>career development through the LMU qualification program and JRC training programme</li> <li>a stimulating working environment at LMU, one of Germany’s top-ranked universities, and at JRC, sitting in the interface between science and policy.</li> <li>organizational assistance for relocation to Munich and to Ispra.</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Please send an application outlining your fit for the position (including a cover letter, a CV, copies of scientific degrees, and the names and contact information of two references) by e-mail (one PDF-attachment with max. 5 MB including all documents) with subject "JRC-2026LMU" to <a href="mailto:climate.jobs@geographie.uni-muenchen.de">climate.jobs@geographie.uni-muenchen.de</a>. Applications received prior to March 16, 2026, will receive full consideration, but the position will remain open until filled. Interviews will take place on March 23, 24 or 27. For further information please contact Prof. Dr. Julia Pongratz (<a href="mailto:julia.pongratz@lmu.de">julia.pongratz@lmu.de</a>) or Dr. Giacomo Grassi (<a href="mailto:giacomo.grassi@ec.europa.eu">giacomo.grassi@ec.europa.eu</a>).</p>

item.title: Research and Teaching Assistant (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Business Administration - Munich School of Management

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-05-15T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Institute for Strategy, Technology and Organization (ISTO) at LMU Munich School of Management conducts academically rigorous and phenomenon-driven research and teaching in the domain of strategy, organization design and platform markets, building on our principal tenets of quantitative management research. We present our research at international conferences and publish in leading journals, offering access to an international research network. We are committed to placing our researchers on the international academic job market. Prior placements include Bocconi University, Copenhagen Business School, IE Madrid, Rotterdam School of Management, Imperial College London, Amsterdam Business School, among others.</p> <p>Our workplace is centrally located in Munich and is very easy to reach by public transport. Our team welcomes new members and we offer you a dynamic, international and academically stimulating environment.</p>

Your qualifications:

<p>You hold an excellent academic record and a Master’s degree or equivalent in Management, Business Administration, Economics, Information Systems, or a related field. In your studies, you will have gained some experience in working with empirical methods, especially large-scale datasets. Ideally, you would have some prior research experience or work experience in a relevant domain, like a research institute or an analytical role in a company.</p> <p>You are intellectually curious, possess strong analytical capabilities, and have a strong interest in pursuing an international academic career. You are enthusiastic about conducting quantitative empirical research motivated by real-life phenomena in the domain of strategy, organization design and platform markets. You complement our team with your strong organizational skills, are proactive and persistent, able to work both independently and collaboratively, and possess excellent English communication skills (written and oral).</p>

Benefits:

<p>The position is initially for two years with an option to extend, with a starting date to be arranged based on mutual agreement, but ideally by 1 September 2026. You will have the opportunity to study towards a PhD at ISTO as part of the position.</p> <p>LMU Munich is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to enhancing the diversity of its faculty. We encourage female candidates to apply.</p>

Contact: <p>Your application should include:</p> <ul> <li>Statement of motivation (max. one page)</li> <li>CV</li> <li>Copies of degree certificates and transcripts</li> <li>Any other relevant materials</li> <li>Please submit your complete application as <strong>one single PDF file</strong> by e-mail to Mrs. Esther Almasdi-Müller: <a href="mailto:e.almasdi-mueller@lmu.de">e.almasdi-mueller@lmu.de</a>.</li> </ul> <p>Deadline for applications: <strong>15 May 2026</strong>. Interviews are scheduled for late June/July 2026.</p>

item.title: Postdoctoral Position in Strategy, Organization and Technology (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Business Administration - Munich School of Management

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-05-15T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:


Your qualifications:

<p>You have completed (or are about to complete) a doctoral degree in a relevant field, have demonstrated outstanding research potential through excellent dissertation research, and enjoy working in diverse and interdisciplinary teams. Ideally, you are working on or interested in strategic, organizational, or technological issues in digital markets, especially platforms and their ecosystems. Your work will draw on quantitative firm- or individual-level data, and some prior exposure to economic models and (lab or field) experimental settings is an advantage.</p>

Benefits:

<p>The position is a fixed-term appointment for two years, with a possibility of extension pending successful evaluation. The starting date for the appointment can be set upon mutual agreement but should be no later than 1st September 2026.</p> <p>A conversion to an indefinite position (tenured) is not possible.</p> <p>ISTO offers a dynamic and international environment, with research and travel budget available for the members of the institute. We are involved in several large-scale research projects with national and international partners. ISTO also participates in the Organizations Research Group (ORG), running a regular seminar series and hosting leading international scholars. You will have the opportunity to collaborate closely with Prof. Daniel Obermeier and Prof. Tobias Kretschmer, who are strongly committed to supporting postdoctoral researchers in their ongoing and future research. This has resulted in publications in leading academic journals, such as Strategic Management Journal, Management Science, Organization Science and Marketing Science, and successful placement of our postdoctoral researchers on the international academic job market. Prior placements of our alumni include Bocconi University, Copenhagen Business School, IE Madrid, Rotterdam School of Management, Imperial College London, University of Amsterdam, among others.</p> <p>Your workplace is centrally located in Munich and is very easy to reach by public transport. LMU Munich provides newly appointed academics with various types of support, including welcome services.</p> <p>We encourage female candidates to apply.</p>

Contact: <p>Your application (in English only) should include:</p> <ul> <li>Statement of motivation (max. one page)</li> <li>CV with publication list</li> <li>Contact details of two referees</li> <li>Job market paper (if available)</li> <li>Copies of degree certificates and transcripts</li> </ul> <p>Please submit your complete application as one single PDF file by e-mail to Ms. Esther Almasdi-Müller: <a href="mailto:e.almasdi-mueller@lmu.de">e.almasdi-mueller@lmu.de</a>.</p> <p><strong>Deadline for applications: 15 May 2026</strong>. On-site interviews are scheduled for late June/July 2026.</p>

item.title: PhD student (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Philosophy, Philosophy of Science and the Study of Religion

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-03-15T22:59:16+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The chair will host the new international project The Mathematical Turn in Philosophy: Measurement, Computation, (De)Idealization, one of the UK-German Research Projects in the Arts and Humanities funded by the DFG and the AHRC. The project seeks to provide a critical framework for addressing the increasing role of mathematics and computation in philosophy in several of its core areas. The objective of the project is to develop a unified methodology for understanding the mathematical turn in contemporary philosophy. The Principal Investigator of the German part is <a href="https://www.philosophie.lmu.de/en/directory-of-persons/contact-page/martin-fischer-76784a68.html">PD Dr. Martin Fischer</a>.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>Candidates must have successfully completed a master program in philosophy and/or mathematics and/or an MSc in computer science. The master degree must have been awarded by the beginning of the contract.</li> <li>Candidates should have a strong mathematical, logical and computational orientation and aptitude.</li> <li>Candidates should be capable of engaging in teamwork.</li> <li>Excellent English language skills are required.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>The salary will be calculated according to group <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">E 13 TVL-employment</a> (65%, part-time). The position is limited to three years</li> <li>Successful applicants will also have the opportunity for an extensive exchange with the University of Warwick, Walter Dean and Benedict Eastaugh.</li> <li>Funds available to attend workshops and conferences.</li> </ul> <p>The Chair is part of the <a href="https://www.mcmp.philosophie.uni-muenchen.de">Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy</a>, which offers a world-class environment for research in formally oriented areas of philosophy. Furthermore, LMU’s Faculty of Philosophy has significant strengths across a wide range of different areas of philosophy, theoretical as well as practical, contemporary as well as historical.</p> <p>We especially encourage women and candidates from underrepresented groups to apply.</p>

Contact: <p>Applications should be written entirely in English and should include:</p> <ul> <li>A cover letter that addresses the candidate’s academic profile and their motivation for applying for the advertised position.</li> <li>A proposal for a dissertation on the project topic `reverse philosophy’ (maximally five pages).</li> <li>A CV with a list of publications and/or PDF-files of unpublished manuscripts, and an academic transcript of records.</li> </ul> <p>These materials should be collated into a single PDF document and sent to <a href="mailto:m.fischer1@lmu.de">m.fischer1@lmu.de</a> <strong>by 15.03.2026</strong>. <em>The subject line of the email should include ``PhD application" and the name of the applicant.</em></p> <p>Furthermore,</p> <ul> <li>two confidential letters of recommendation should also be sent directly to <a href="mailto:m.fischer1@lmu.de">m.fischer1@lmu.de</a> <strong>by 15.03.2026</strong></li> </ul>

item.title: Research and Teaching Assistant (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Business Administration - Munich School of Management

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-05-31T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Institute for Financial Innovation and Technology (FinTech) at LMU Munich School of Management conducts academically rigorous, relevant and exciting research and teaching in the domain of financial innovation and technology (FinTech). We cover topics like market microstructure, high frequency trading, cryptocurrencies & blockchain, tokenomics, financial data science and the application of machine learning in capital markets. We present our research at international conferences and publish in leading journals. We will also collaborate directly with the financial industry and the local FinTech scene. Our workplace is centrally located in Munich and is very easy to reach by public transport. Our team welcomes new members, and we offer you a dynamic, international and academically stimulating environment.</p>

Your qualifications:

<p>You hold an excellent academic record and a Master’s degree or equivalent in Finance, Management, Business Administration, Economics, Business Informatics, Business Math, Computer Science, or a related field. In your studies, you will have gained some experience in working with empirical methods, especially large and complex datasets. You are intellectually curious, possess strong analytical capabilities, and are a competent programmer in Python, and/or R. You complement our team with your strong organizational skills, are proactive and persistent, able to work both independently and collaboratively, and possess excellent English communication skills (written and oral).</p>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Company pension scheme</li> <li>Capital-forming benefits</li> <li>Christmas bonus</li> <li>Work-life balance: <ul> <li>Flexible working hours</li> <li>Childcare support (e.g. holiday and emergency childcare)</li> <li>30 days of vacation plus days off on December 24 and 31</li> </ul> </li> <li>Training and continuing education program at all career levels</li> <li>Participation in specialist conferences and conventions</li> <li>Global exchange opportunities and internships at one of our 600 international partner universities</li> <li>Health promotion offers</li> <li>A crisis-proof job</li> <li>Mobility: discounted local transport tickets, job bikes, and charging stations for electric cars</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Your application should include:</p> <ul> <li>Statement of motivation (max. one page)</li> <li>CV</li> <li>Copies of degree certificates and transcripts</li> <li>Any other relevant materials.</li> </ul> <p>Please submit your complete application as one single PDF file (max. 10 MB) by e-mail to Professor Riordan (<a href="mailto:fintech@som.lmu.de">fintech@som.lmu.de</a>).</p> <p><strong>Deadline for applications: 31 May 2026</strong>. Interviews are scheduled to be held in June 2026. If you have any questions, please contact Dr. Luca Galati at <a href="mailto:Luca.Galati@lmu.de">Luca.Galati@lmu.de</a>.</p>
